about: The one masker's table (packages/mask-secrets/src/secrets.json): [text, masked] pairs that the Rust (tasks.rs), page (packages/mask-secrets/test/secrets.test.ts) and bridge (test_bridge.py OneMasker) tests all run. Every token here is synthetic. The last fourteen are the length rule (PR #2908 verify9): a gh?_ body of exactly 36 or a glpat- body of exactly 20, split by line breaks or a space, in upper, mixed, lower case or digits, is masked whole; prose after a short prefix mention stays. Item 113 added the rest: private key blocks (RSA, EC, OpenSSH, PGP, SSH2, unended, and inside a JSON string), provider prefixes (Stripe, Google, Slack app, npm, Hugging Face, PyPI, Shopify, DigitalOcean, GitLab runner, Groq, Supabase, Linear, Notion, Omise, SendGrid, AWS ASIA, Telegram), JSON web tokens, credentials in HTTP headers (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, X-Api-Key and the like, a lone Bearer, Cookie), `password:` and `"password":` in YAML and JSON, `scheme://user:pass@host`, quoted `KEY="..."`, and `--password value` on a command line, each beside an ordinary line it must not mangle (hex colours, a git SHA, a UUID, base64 of an image, the word in prose, a TypeScript type). Bodies are made-up X's or counted runs, short of any provider's real length where the rule allows, so no scanner reads them as live keys. Item 121: a `command` row's third field names the notes its card adds (`unmasked`: shown as it is, since masking it could change what it seems to do), and its rows hold blanks, stray quotes, `#`, globs and key blocks the shell would run; every row's shown line must split into as many shell words as the command. `shape` rows are [command, a masked line, whether the structural check lets that line be shown].
